title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 17
paragraphs: Having said this, Artabanus — expecting that he would prove Xerxes's words to be folly — did as he was bidden, and having put on Xerxes's robes and seated himself on the royal throne, afterwards lay down in the royal bed. When he had fallen asleep, the same dream that used to come to Xerxes came to him too, and standing over Artabanus it spoke these words: “So you are the man, are you, who is trying to turn Xerxes aside from marching against Greece, pretending to care for him? Neither in the future nor now in the present shall you go unpunished for trying to divert what is destined to happen; and as for Xerxes, what he must suffer if he disobeys has already been made clear to the man himself.”
